title: When limestone lets go
hook: Breaking limestone soaks up heat. So can it ever happen by itself, and when?

doesNotKnow: that a change goes by itself when ΔH − TΔS is negative
that a heat-absorbing change that makes gas therefore switches on above a definite temperature

misconception: A reaction that absorbs heat can never go by itself; heating only 'feeds it' gradually, with no switch point.
objective: The learner can say that limestone's breakdown switches on near 850 °C (about 845 °C from 25 °C data), where TΔS grows past ΔH, and explain that making a gas raises entropy and temperature multiplies that gain.

claims.text: Standard values at 25 °C: ΔfH CaCO3 (calcite) −1,207.6, CaO −634.9, CO2 −393.51 kJ/mol; S° CaCO3 91.7, CaO 38.1, CO2 213.79 J/(mol K) (inputs to every number on the stage).
claims.source: CRC Handbook, standard thermodynamic properties of chemical substances; CODATA Key Values for Thermodynamics (1989) for CaO and CO2. Calcite values differ by about 1 kJ/mol between tables; the crossover moves by under 10 °C. Brief claim 1.
claims.note: Opened: the CRC table (chemicals 1.5.2) gives calcite -1,207.6 and 91.7, CaO -634.9 and 38.1, CO2 -393.5 and 213.8. JANAF 1998 gives CO2 -393.522 and 213.795. CODATA not opened; the -393.51 and 213.79 figures agree. 'Calcite differs by about 1 kJ/mol between tables' checked: NASA TM-4513 (Barin 89) gives -1,206.9 and 92.9; with those, the crossover moves by under 1 °C.

claims.text: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 absorbs about 179 kJ/mol (ΔH° +179) and raises entropy by about 160 J/(mol K) (stage label 'ΔH (heat in): 179 kJ'; question: 'absorbing heat'; reveal: 'the 179 kJ of heat needed', 'Making a gas raises entropy').
claims.source: ΔH° = −634.9 − 393.51 + 1,207.6 = +179.19 kJ/mol; ΔS° = 38.1 + 213.79 − 91.7 = +160.19 J/(mol K) (node, demo-builder 2026-10-14; Demo.tsx DH, DS), from claim 1. Brief claim 2.
claims.note: Derivation re-run: dH = +179.19 kJ/mol, dS = +160.19 J/(mol K).

claims.text: A change at constant temperature and pressure goes by itself when ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is negative (stage: 'does not go' / 'goes by itself'; reveal: 'ΔG was +131 kJ and nothing happened', 'ΔG was −9 kJ and limestone breaks up by itself').
claims.source: Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry, the Gibbs energy (spontaneity at constant T and p). Brief claim 3. Here ΔG° at 1 bar CO2 (the question states 1 bar CO2).
claims.note: Verified on derivation (Atkins not opened): at constant T and p the second law gives dG <= 0 for a spontaneous change. The stage applies dG° at 1 bar CO2, the condition stated in the question.

claims.text: With 25 °C values held constant, TΔS is about 48, 124 and 188 kJ/mol at 25, 500 and 900 °C, so ΔG° is about +131, +55 and −9 kJ/mol (stage labels 'TΔS at 900 °C: 188 kJ', readouts 'ΔG at 25 °C +131 kJ', 'ΔG at 900 °C −9 kJ'; reveal: '+131 kJ', '−9 kJ').
claims.note: Derivation re-run: TdS 47.76, 123.85 and 187.93; dG +131.43, +55.34 and -8.74. The stated model is on the stage ('(25 °C data)' on the switch label). With the full NASA TM-4513 data, dG° is +130.9, +57.7 and -1.0 kJ/mol: the signs and verdicts are unchanged. Non-blocking: the 900 °C readout shows -9 kJ where the full data give about -1 kJ, so the '(25 °C data)' caveat could also go next to the dG readouts.

claims.text: With 25 °C values held constant, ΔG° = 0 near 845 °C, an estimate (stage: 'switch ≈ 845 °C (25 °C data)'; reveal: 'The switch sits near 845 °C, where TΔS equals ΔH'; right option 'about 850 °C'). Measured decomposition at 1 bar CO2 is about 890 °C.
claims.source: T = 179,190 / 160.19 = 1,118.6 K = 845.4 °C (node; Demo.tsx T_SWITCH). The 890 °C figure: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, calcium chapter, or CRC (dissociation pressure of CaCO3 against temperature); it is not shown to the learner. If it cannot be checked, drop that sentence and keep 'about 850 °C, an estimate'. Brief claim 4.
claims.note: Split. Part 1 verified on derivation: 179,190/160.19 = 1,118.6 K = 845.5 °C, shown as 845 °C and labelled '(25 °C data)'. Part 2 ('Measured decomposition at 1 bar CO2 is about 890 °C') held: Greenwood & Earnshaw and the CRC dissociation-pressure table could not be opened. In node, the NASA TM-4513 polynomials (calcite BAR 89, CaO J 6/73, CO2 L 7/88) give dG° = 0 at 893 °C. That is consistent with 890 °C, but it is evaluated data, not the cited measurement. Fix: drop the 'measured' sentence (the brief's instruction), or reword it to 'full-temperature data (NASA TM-4513, McBride et al. 1993) put dG° = 0 near 893 °C' and I will verify. The right option 'about 850 °C' is still the nearest at 893 °C.

claims.text: Temperature multiplies the entropy gain (TΔS); absorbing heat does not forbid a change, it sets the temperature where it starts (reveal).
claims.source: From ΔG = ΔH − TΔS with ΔH > 0 and ΔS > 0: ΔG < 0 exactly when T > ΔH/ΔS (Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry). Claims 2-5.
claims.note: Derivation: with dH > 0 and dS > 0, dG < 0 exactly when T > dH/dS.

recall.question: A change absorbs heat but turns a solid into a gas. What happens as you heat it?
options: It can never go by itself, because it absorbs heat
It goes by itself above some temperature, where TΔS outgrows ΔH
It goes by itself at any temperature, a little faster when hot
recall.why: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. Making gas raises entropy, and TΔS grows with temperature, so above T = ΔH/ΔS the change goes by itself. Limestone switches near 850 °C.
